name: manual_22d75f
claim: Keep a shared defaults file in JSON when every consumer is stdlib-only and a vendored copy must be a plain byte-stable copy: JSON has one canonical form for fingerprints and no implicit typing, at the cost of comments, so explanations live in description and note fields; protect the vendored copy with a self-checking stamp (source fingerprint, source date, copy date) and report stale, old and hand-edited copies at start-up, with the sync itself waiting for a human to confirm.

decisions.notes: Operator decisions 2026-11-27 and the side agent's stale-copy warning: the OpenClaw defaults file is JSON, its vendored copy carries a verifiable stamp, and syncing needs human confirmation.

rationale: Operator decisions 2026-11-27 and the side agent's stale-copy warning: the OpenClaw defaults file is JSON, its vendored copy carries a verifiable stamp, and syncing needs human confirmation.
